keyVerseText: And this shall be a sign unto thee, Ye shall eat this year such things as grow of themselves, and in the second year that which springeth of the same; and in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruits thereof.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שָׁחִיס (shâchîyç) derives from an apparently unused root that likely means 'to sprout.' This etymology highlights the concept of something that grows spontaneously, without human planting, emphasizing natural or automatic growth. The literal sense of 'that which springeth' conveys the idea of an aftergrowth or volunteer grain that appears in the second year without being sown again, distinguishing it from cultivated crops.
usageInScripture: The term שָׁחִיס appears only twice in Scripture and consistently carries the meaning of 'that which springeth' or volunteer grain. Its usage is tightly focused on describing grain that grows of itself in the second year, as seen in 2 Kings 19:29 and Isaiah 37:30. This consistency reveals the word's specialized agricultural context, underscoring God's provision through unexpected or unplanned growth.
theologicalSignificance: The concept of שָׁחִיס as grain that grows by itself without human effort points to God's sovereign provision and faithfulness, even in times of scarcity or judgment. It reminds believers that God can sustain His people through unexpected means, providing nourishment and hope beyond human planning. This word enriches our understanding of divine grace as active in the natural order, sustaining life through what springs forth spontaneously. It encourages trust in God's care, highlighting His ability to bless and restore even when circumstances seem dire.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 19:29, the promise that 'ye shall eat this year such things as grow of themselves, and in the second year that which springeth of the same' uses שָׁחִיס to emphasize God's provision during a time of crisis. The word captures the idea of food arising naturally without deliberate planting, symbolizing God's miraculous sustenance. This verse reassures believers that God governs the cycles of provision, allowing life to continue through His faithful care even in hardship.
